(C) \([Fe(CN)_{6}]^{4-}\) is \(Fe^{2+}\) \(d^{6}\) with the strong-field cyanide, so \(t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}\), low spin. (D) \([Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}\) is \(Co^{3+}\) \(d^{6}\) with ammonia, which for the highly charged \(Co^{3+}\) is sufficient to force pairing, so it is also low spin. Hence only (C) and (D).
authoredSolutions.118: Toluene with chromyl chloride in carbon disulphide undergoes the Etard reaction, and hydrolysis of the chromium complex with \(H_{3}O^{+}\) gives benzaldehyde. Adding sodium bisulphite then converts the aldehyde into its crystalline bisulphite addition compound, \(C_{6}H_{5}-CH(OH)-SO_{3}Na\), which is insoluble and is collected on filtration, so this is residue (A). Warming the adduct with dilute HCl reverses the addition and regenerates the free aldehyde, so compound (B) is benzaldehyde. This bisulphite sequence is the standard way of separating an aldehyde from unreacted toluene, which is why toluene is used in excess.
authoredSolutions.119: Statement (I) is true: corrosion is an electrochemical process in which the pure, more active metal region behaves as the anode and is oxidised, while the impurity-rich region acts as the cathode where oxygen is reduced, the moisture film acting as the electrolyte. Statement (II) is false: the cathodic reduction \(O_{2} + 4H^{+} + 4e^{-} \rightarrow 2H_{2}O\) consumes hydrogen ions, so by the Nernst equation its potential and hence the driving force for corrosion FALL as the pH rises. Corrosion is therefore faster in acidic than in alkaline medium, which is why alkaline passivation is used for protection.
authoredSolutions.120: A secondary hydrogen sits on a carbon attached to exactly two other carbons, so each secondary \(CH_{2}\) contributes two of them; exactly two secondary hydrogens therefore means exactly one \(CH_{2}\) group flanked by two carbons. In 2,2,3,3-tetramethylpentane, \(CH_{3}-C(CH_{3})_{2}-C(CH_{3})_{2}-CH_{2}-CH_{3}\), the only such group is C-4, giving exactly two secondary hydrogens. By contrast 2,2,4,4-tetramethylhexane has two methylene groups (C-3 and C-5), i.e. four; 2,2,4,5-tetramethylheptane has methylenes at C-3 and C-6, again four; and 4-ethyl-3,4-dimethyloctane has five methylene groups, i.e. ten.
authoredSolutions.121: \(C_{6}H_{6}\) has four degrees of unsaturation. Taking up four moles of hydrogen means all four degrees are pi bonds and none is a ring, which immediately excludes benzene (a ring plus three pi bonds, so only three moles of \(H_{2}\)). Giving only ONE monobromo derivative demands that every hydrogen be equivalent. The compound satisfying both is hexa-2,4-diyne, \(CH_{3}-C\equiv C-C\equiv C-CH_{3}\): its six hydrogens all belong to the two equivalent methyl groups, and its two triple bonds contain four pi bonds, which consume four moles of hydrogen on complete hydrogenation to hexane. Four pi bonds carry \(4 \times 2 = 8\) pi electrons.

authoredSolutions.123: Dimethylglyoxime is \(CH_{3}-C(=NOH)-C(=NOH)-CH_{3}\), \(C_{4}H_{8}N_{2}O_{2}\).
